---
title: "Get started"
---

## Install

The extension asks for Quarto 1.9.36 or later. Each change to it is tested
with Quarto 1.9.36 and with Quarto's current release. In the folder of your project, run:

```bash
quarto add jmgirard/wrapped
```

This command puts the extension under `_extensions/`. Then add the filter
to the document's YAML header:

```yaml
filters:
  - wrapped
```

## Wrap a figure

Add the class `.wrap-right` or `.wrap-left` to a figure. The class names
the side that the figure goes to. The paragraphs after the figure flow
beside it. Each form below shows its source, then the result.

### A captioned figure from a markdown image

```markdown
![Mean ratings by condition.](ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right width="40%"}
```

::: demo
![Mean ratings by condition.](images/ratings.png){#fig-ratings .wrap-right width="40%"}

The image form is the shortest. The text in the square brackets is the
caption, and the `#fig-` id gives the figure its number, so this text can
point to @fig-ratings.

The paragraphs after the figure flow beside it until the text passes the
bottom of the figure. Then they run the full width of the column.
:::

### A captioned figure from a div

```markdown
::: {#fig-groups .wrap-left width="35%"}
![](groups.png)

Ratings by group.
:::
```

::: demo
::: {#fig-groups .wrap-left width="35%"}
![](images/groups.png)

Ratings by group.
:::

The div form puts the caption in the last paragraph of the div, which
keeps a long caption easy to read in the source. The class `.wrap-left` puts the figure on
the left, and this text flows on its right.

@fig-groups has a width of 35%, so the text beside it has a little more
room than beside a figure at the default 40%.
:::

### An image with no caption

```markdown
![](logo.png){.wrap-right width="20%" fig-alt="Lab logo"}
```

::: demo
![](images/badge.png){.wrap-right width="20%" fig-alt="Lab logo"}

An image with no caption wraps too. It gets no figure number. The
`fig-alt` attribute gives it alt text.

The same rules about width and gap apply to it as to a captioned figure.
:::

An image that is the only content of a link, with the link alone in its
paragraph, wraps too, and it keeps its link. Put the wrap class on the
image, not on the link:

```markdown
[![](logo.png){.wrap-right width="20%" fig-alt="Lab logo"}](https://example.com)
```

### A figure from a code cell

Give the cell a `fig-` label and a `fig-cap`, so that Quarto makes a figure.
Put the class in `#| classes:`, and set the width with `#| out-width:`:

::: demo
```{r}
#| echo: fenced
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatter plot."
#| classes: wrap-right
#| out-width: "30%"
plot(1:10)
```

The plot from the cell above floats to the right, and this paragraph
flows beside it. The cell's code stays above the figure, at the full width
of the column.

@fig-scatter is 30% of the text column wide, as `#| out-width:` asks.
:::

The [examples](examples/index.qmd) show each of these forms rendered in
HTML, in PDF through LaTeX, in PDF through Typst, and in Word.

## Wrap a table

A table float wraps in HTML, in PDF through LaTeX, in PDF through Typst,
and in Word. A table float is a table with a `#tbl-` label. A table that an
R package such as gt writes as raw LaTeX or raw Word XML keeps its normal
layout in that format, and the render prints one warning for each table.
Put the class and the width on a `#tbl-` div:

```markdown
::: {#tbl-means .wrap-right width="45%"}

| Condition | Mean | SD  |
|-----------|------|-----|
| A         | 3.1  | 0.4 |
| B         | 4.2  | 0.6 |

: Mean ratings by condition.

:::
```

::: demo
::: {#tbl-means .wrap-right width="45%"}

| Condition | Mean | SD  |
|-----------|------|-----|
| A         | 3.1  | 0.4 |
| B         | 4.2  | 0.6 |

: Mean ratings by condition.

:::

@tbl-means floats to the right, and this paragraph flows beside it. The
caption and the table share the box, at 45% of the text column.

The same rules about width, gap, and where wrapping stops apply to a table
as to a figure.
:::

The class can also go in the attribute block at the end of the caption:

- A pipe table with its id in the block, as in
  `: Mean ratings by condition. {#tbl-means .wrap-right width="45%"}`.
  The block can also hold `width` and `wrap-gap`.
- A block inside a `#tbl-` div, as in `: Mean ratings by condition. {.wrap-right}`.
  Put a `width` or `wrap-gap` for this form on the div.
- A code cell with a `tbl-` label: the class goes in `#| classes:`, or in a
  block at the end of `#| tbl-cap:`. A code cell table takes the width and
  gap of the [document defaults](defaults.qmd). In Word, a table from gt
  or flextable keeps its normal layout (see
  [Word](formats/word.qmd#tables)). In PDF through LaTeX, a table from gt,
  kableExtra, or tinytable keeps its normal layout (see
  [PDF through LaTeX](formats/latex.qmd#tables)).
